          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 9
        
      
                          
                      Oct 29, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Gameweek 9 awaits in Fantasy Premier League, and The 10% Club returns with five more under-the-radar picks.
João Pedro’s injury and Cole Palmer’s red card dampened many Fantasy Premier League plans last weekend, but we have some solutions here in The 10% Club.
There are some interesting differential options for Gameweek 9, including a Bournemouth defender, a surprising Tottenham choice, and a striker who has only just come back into the fold.
Using Opta data, we’ve picked out five under-the-radar gems – all in fewer than 10% of squads worldwide – that could get you ahead of your mini-league rivals.
With David Raya proving his worth as the most expensive, highest owned, and top-scoring goalkeeper, many FPL managers will be settled on the Arsenal man.
However, there is a differential option should you wish to go against the template when Mikel Arteta’s champions have a tough trip to Liverpool at Anfield this week.
After ending Manchester City’s perfect start last Saturday, a favourable run sees Aston Villa face Fulham (H), Manchester United (A), Sunderland (H), Ipswich Town (A) and Everton (H).
So, we’d suggest looking at Zion Suzuki as a different selection between the posts. The Japanese goalkeeper may rank eighth for points (30) in his position, but there is a key caveat.

Suzuki has finished in the bonus points (3 against Hull City, 2 against Newcastle United) whenever Villa have kept a clean sheet this season (twice). More shutouts could be likely with a friendlier set of fixtures, too.
Averaging 3.6 saves per 90 minutes, Suzuki is also a strong contender for at least one additional point that FPL awards goalkeepers for a minimum of three saves per match.
Plus, after Johan Manzambi (11 points on GW7) and Nicolas Jackson (13 points on GW8) delivered for this column, you don’t want to miss out on another Villa pick.
Bournemouth may have endured a tough start to life under Marco Rose, but there have been signs of revival in the last two weeks.

Rose’s side earned their first win and clean sheet of the season with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Sunderland on GW7, before hammering Manchester United 3-0 on GW8. They also beat Milan 3-0 in the UEFA Europa League in between those league victories.
So, having already highlighted the potential of Marcus Tavernier (GW5) and Evanilson (GW7), we’re now considering Bournemouth’s defence.

António Silva has secured an additional two points for defensive contributions in six of eight games so far. No defender can better his 75% DEFCON hit rate either, while he is £0.5m cheaper than teammate James Hill for largely the same points output.

Leeds United’s visit should see Silva tested in duels by FPL favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin, before a presentable run of fixtures boost his chances of a clean sheet against Ipswich (A), Nottingham Forest (H) and Fulham (A).
Brighton’s Luka Vuskovic (52 points) and Maxim De Cuyper (60) are in a similar price bracket, but with the Seagulls away to Man City, Silva is our defender locked in for this weekend.
Much like Silva, Kristoffer Ajer is another reliable defensive option for Brentford ahead of their home clash with Forest.

Although Ajer has reached the DEFCON threshold in just three of his eight games, he has been close to greater success. Ajer finished one short of 10 defensive contributions in three straight matches against Bournemouth, Chelsea and Villa.
The Norwegian defender also chipped in with his first goal of the season in that Villa draw, and he remains a consistent threat from both corners and throw-ins with Brentford’s set-piece proficiency.
